data.why: The repository ships three reference jsPsych specs (flanker, shapes, stroop) meant to be opened in the builder via 'Open a project...', so no synthetic data is needed.

goals: Build a cognitive task (e.g. a flanker or Stroop paradigm) from scratch using the no-code timeline, stimuli and conditions-table editor
Open an existing study spec (examples/flanker.json, shapes.json or stroop.json) and inspect/modify its timeline, branching and conditions
Preview the experiment live in the sandboxed frame to confirm stimuli, timing and branching behave as intended before deploying
Configure data handling (DataPipe upload, save-on-end vs stream, recruitment platform parameters) for a study destined for real participants
Export the finished experiment as a single HTML file or a zipped project ready to host
Inspect the generated jsPsych source as the study is edited, to confirm the compiled code matches the intended design

review.summary: This is an accurate, well-ordered tree for building, previewing and exporting a jsPsych study, and most cited screens show what the nodes say. Before filing it needs tasks for group assignment and counterbalancing, early endings and adding your own media, a split of the data/recruitment and code/export bundles, and a fix or note for the broken Stroop scoring example.
